about: Five fictional ventures answered through the customer form (treadle.form/1). Each probes one kind of business or one kind of difficulty. Kept fixed so a scorecard before and after a change compares like with like.

cases.probe: physical local business with concrete prices, capacity and costs

answers.description: A specialty coffee shop on NW 23rd Avenue in Portland, Oregon. Espresso and pour-over, a small pastry case, about 15 seats. Mostly locals and people working on laptops. Drinks are around six dollars.
answers.status_quo: Other neighbourhood cafes, Starbucks two blocks away, and making coffee at home or at the office.
answers.monthly_cost_estimate: About $28,000 a month: rent $7,500, two baristas and a manager about $14,000, beans and milk $4,000, utilities and the rest $2,500.
answers.customer_evidence: We ran a weekend pop-up for a month and sold about 120 drinks a day; people liked the pour-over and asked for more seating.
answers.named_competitors: Barista on NW 13th and Coava Coffee.
answers.success_target: Around $450,000 in the first year, roughly 200 drinks a day.
answers.business_model: Pay per item: drinks and pastries.
answers.geography: NW 23rd Avenue, Portland, Oregon. People will walk 10 minutes or drive about 2 miles.
answers.service_capacity: About 300 drinks a day at most with two baristas.
answers.scalability: Fixed capacity at one site; a second site would need its own lease and staff.
answers.acquisition_channels: Foot traffic, Instagram, and word of mouth from regulars.
answers.unit_economics: A $6 latte costs about $1.40 in beans, milk and cup.
answers.fixed_costs: Rent $7,500 a month, salaries about $14,000 a month, equipment lease $600 a month.
answers.constraints: Needs a Multnomah County food service licence; the lease limits signage.

cases.probe: online B2B subscription with a named buyer and price

answers.description: A scheduling tool for small physiotherapy clinics. They pay monthly per practitioner. Right now they run on paper diaries and a lot of phone calls, and no-shows cost them a fortune.
answers.status_quo: Paper diaries, Google Calendar, and general practice systems like Jane App.
answers.monthly_cost_estimate: About $9,000 a month: two developers part time and hosting.
answers.customer_evidence: Three clinics are piloting it for free and say no-shows dropped.
answers.success_target: 100 paying clinics in the first year.
answers.scalability: Scales easily; support is the bottleneck.
answers.acquisition_channels: Physio association newsletters, Google search, and referrals between clinics.
answers.unit_economics: Hosting and SMS reminders cost about $3 per practitioner per month.
answers.fixed_costs: Developer time and about $400 a month in software subscriptions.
answers.constraints: Patient data means HIPAA compliance in the US.

cases.probe: two-sided marketplace with a cold-start problem

answers.description: An app where dog owners book local walkers. We take a cut of each booking. The hard part is getting enough walkers signed up in one neighbourhood before owners will trust it.
answers.status_quo: Rover, Wag, asking neighbours, or friends walking the dog.
answers.business_model: We take 20% of each booking; a 30 minute walk costs about $25.
answers.delivery_mode: A mix: booked online, walked in person.
answers.geography: Launching in the Annex and Little Italy neighbourhoods of Toronto.
answers.acquisition_channels: Flyers in dog parks, Instagram, and referral credit for both sides.
answers.constraints: Walkers need insurance and a background check.

cases.probe: a one-line brief with every question skipped

answers.description: An app that helps people be more productive.

cases.probe: answers that contradict the description and each other

answers.description: An online-only subscription meal-planning service for busy parents, $20 a month, delivered entirely through our app across the US.
answers.monthly_cost_estimate: About $2,000 a month in total: rent is $5,000 and salaries are $10,000.
answers.business_model: Customers pay $5 per meal plan, one at a time.
answers.delivery_mode: In person, at our kitchen in Chicago.
answers.success_target: 10 million subscribers in the first year.
answers.service_capacity: We can serve about 50 families a week.
